name: GLCM Texture Analysis
description: Analyzes spatial relationships between pixel intensity levels using Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix. AI images show smoother textures with higher homogeneity.
algorithm: Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) + Haralick Features
mechanism: Computes GLCM and extracts contrast, energy, and homogeneity features. AI-generated images have higher homogeneity and energy.
parameters: Levels: 16, Distance: 1, Angle: 0 degrees, Features: contrast/energy/homogeneity
useCase: Detecting overly smooth textures in AI-generated content

references.title: Haralick, R.M. et al. (1973). Textural Features for Image Classification. IEEE TSMC.
Clausi, D.A. (2002). An Analysis of Co-occurrence Texture Statistics. Canadian J. Remote Sensing.
Fridrich, J. & Kodovsky, J. (2012). Rich Models for Steganalysis. IEEE TIFS.

strengths:
• Well-established statistical texture descriptor since 1973
• Captures spatial pixel relationships at multiple distances
• Provides multiple complementary features (contrast, energy, correlation)
• Rotation-invariant with multi-angle analysis
• Low false positive rate for texture anomalies
limitations:
• Computationally expensive for large distance parameters
• Parameter selection (distance, angle) significantly impacts results
• Sensitive to image noise and compression artifacts
• Quantization of gray levels reduces discriminative power
• High-quality AI textures may pass GLCM analysis
